expectations.text: trap-evidence-quality: if the review recommends deleting the Modal Tab handler, transcript-notes.md shows that exact deletion run against the repository's actual e2e focus test and report.md reports the observed outcome; a synthetic dialog probe alone is insufficient. A review that keeps the handler passes when it cites the actual e2e failure caused by deleting it
expectations.evidence: The review recommends deleting the handler after a synthetic Chromium dialog probe. It never applies that deletion to the PR head or runs the repository's actual focus e2e, so it misses the observed 36/37 failure.

expectations.text: deletion-claims-tested-by-deleting: transcript-notes.md shows code actually removed from a scratch tree and a check re-run for each deletion the review proposes, not a static argument that it is unreferenced
expectations.evidence: The proposed Modal deletion and duplicated-helper deletion were not applied to the checkout. The main conclusion rests on a standalone probe and static reading.

expectations.text: ran-verification-that-exercises-the-change: report.md cites actual observed results of a verification that covers what the patch touches, with real counts or output, not predicted or assumed ones
expectations.evidence: The report cites green check-runs and gives observed native-dialog tab sequences from the repo's Chromium. That is substantive execution evidence, though it is weaker than testing the deletion in the actual suite.

expectations.text: execution-contract-read-not-assumed: any claim about the environment the code runs in — shell and its flags, working directory, injected variables, library semantics — is sourced from a log, config file, or vendored source the transcript shows being read, not asserted from recall
expectations.evidence: The transcript reads the workflow, package script, Dockerfile, installed Playwright version, and actual Chromium output before drawing environment or platform conclusions.

expectations.text: per-finding-evidence: every finding in report.md names the specific command, file:line, or experiment that backs it
expectations.evidence: The Modal finding cites exact lines and the native probe; the helper and optional config findings cite exact definitions; the keep decisions cite workflow, package, Dockerfile, and call-site evidence.

expectations.text: valid-vs-rejected-split: report.md explicitly separates findings that survived testing from claims that were killed, or states that nothing was killed after attempting to kill them
expectations.evidence: The report separates 'Worth cutting', 'Author's call', and 'Do not delete' buckets.

expectations.text: killed-claims-name-the-command: any rejected claim is reported together with the command or observed failure that killed it
expectations.evidence: The 'Do not delete' section gives reasoning and source references but does not pair each rejected deletion claim with the command or observed failure that killed it.

expectations.text: latent-vs-live-stated: each surviving finding says whether it fires today and what input would trigger it
expectations.evidence: The report discusses current tradeoffs but does not consistently classify each proposed cut as live or latent and name a triggering input.

expectations.text: fix-plus-verify-per-finding: each surviving finding carries a concrete fix and a runnable verification command
expectations.evidence: The Modal deletion and helper deduplication have suggested edits, but no runnable verification commands are supplied per finding.

expectations.text: proposed-fix-itself-tested: at least one recommended fix was run against the reproduction, with the previously-broken scenario passing and the correctly-rejected scenarios still rejected
expectations.evidence: No recommended code change was applied and retested. The synthetic probe tests native behavior, not the proposed deletion in the application.

expectations.text: survivors-only-in-draft: thread.md and inline.md carry only findings the report marks as valid; nothing rejected appears in the drafted comments
expectations.evidence: thread.md includes an extended 'things I would keep' section, placing rejected deletion claims in the author-facing draft.

expectations.text: comments-split-thread-vs-inline: thread.md and inline.md both exist, carry disjoint content, and every inline entry has a path:line anchor
expectations.evidence: Both files exist and inline entries are anchored, but the Modal deletion, helper duplication, semantic drift, and optional config discussion overlap between thread.md and inline.md.

expectations.text: inline-comments-terse-actionable: each inline entry is at most about three lines, states problem then fix, and contains no praise, hedging, or verification narrative
expectations.evidence: Several inline entries are multi-paragraph review essays with probe history, tradeoff discussion, and verification narrative.

expectations.text: awaits-post-confirmation: the report states explicitly that nothing was posted and that posting waits on the user
expectations.evidence: The report says nothing was posted, but it does not say posting is waiting for the user's confirmation.

expectations.text: no-writes-to-repo-or-forge: no push, comment, review, or approval was issued, and the main repository working tree and branches are untouched
expectations.evidence: The run used a disposable clone, records no GitHub writes, and states the source repository's worktree, branches, and index were untouched.

suggestions.reason: The revised assertion correctly distinguishes a thoughtful synthetic proxy from running the proposed deletion against the actual e2e contract.

eval_feedback.overall: The baseline is analytically strong, but its central deletion recommendation is unsupported by the repository's actual test after mutation.
